title: Toyota Launches 9th-Generation Hilux in India Starting at Rs 31.99 Lakh
excerpt: The iconic pickup truck gets a bold 'Cyber Sumo' redesign, a first-ever 4x2 variant, and a cabin packed with new tech — with test drives beginning July 29.
body:
• Toyota has launched the 9th-generation Hilux in India at Rs 31.99–36.69 lakh (ex-showroom), with test drives starting July 29
  • A 4x2 drivetrain option is available for the first time, lowering the entry point for buyers who don't need off-road capability
  • The cabin receives dual 12.3-inch screens, a JBL audio system, and advanced safety tech including Blind Spot Monitor and Pre-collision Safety
  • The 2.8-litre turbo-diesel engine returns with 204 PS and 500 Nm, paired exclusively with a 6-speed automatic transmission

A Ground-Up Redesign for a Global Workhorse

Toyota Kirloskar Motor (TKM) has taken the wraps off the 9th-generation Hilux in India, pricing the lifestyle pickup from Rs 31.99 lakh for the new GX 4x2 AT variant to Rs 36.69 lakh for the range-topping VX 4x4 AT, both ex-showroom. The launch, which took place on July 28, arrives roughly eight months after the truck's global debut, according to MotorBeam.

The most striking change sits up front. Toyota calls the new face the "Cyber Sumo" design, inspired by the pre-combat Sikhiri stance of sumo wrestlers. Slimmer LED headlamps with integrated DRLs flank a squared-off grille that now spells out 'TOYOTA' in bold lettering, replacing the traditional badge. A silver skid plate and circular fog lamps round out a bumper that looks distinctly more aggressive than its predecessor, according to CarToq.

First-Ever 4x2 Option Broadens Appeal

For the first time in the Hilux's history in India, Toyota is offering a 4x2 drivetrain configuration. The previous generation was exclusively 4x4, which kept the price — and the target audience — limited. The new GX 4x2 AT base variant brings the starting price below Rs 32 lakh, a move aimed at buyers who want a lifestyle pickup for urban and highway use without the full off-road hardware.

The 4x4 variants continue with rugged hardware and electronics, including selectable drive and terrain modes. Toyota is also offering a wide catalogue of accessories and add-ons for customisation, according to CarToq.

Tech-Loaded Cabin, Safety Overhaul

Inside, the redesign is just as comprehensive. A freestanding 12.3-inch touchscreen infotainment unit with wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto takes centre stage, paired with a 9-speaker JBL premium audio system. The instrument cluster is now a 10.25-inch digital display, and four USB Type-C ports are scattered through the cabin, according to GaadiWaadi.

The safety package marks a generational leap. New features include a Driver Monitor Camera, Blind Spot Monitor, Safe Exit Assist, Proactive Driving Assist, a Pre-collision Safety system, and a cabin detection alert, per GaadiWaadi. The Hilux also gains electric power steering, replacing the heavy hydraulic unit from the outgoing model — a change that should make city driving noticeably easier.

"Toyota has based the 9th generation of the Hilux on its 'QDR' philosophy — Quality, Durability and Reliability. This has remained the core strength of the truck for decades."

— Toyota Kirloskar Motor

Familiar Powertrain, Upgraded Platform

Under the bonnet, the proven 2.8-litre four-cylinder turbo-diesel engine returns, producing 204 PS and 500 Nm of torque. It is mated to a 6-speed torque converter automatic gearbox. The 9th-generation truck sits on a heavily upgraded version of Toyota's globally proven IMV platform, with reworked suspension tuned for a better ride-handling balance, according to CarToq.

CarDekho had earlier reported that the India-spec Hilux could also receive the 48-volt mild-hybrid system found on the Toyota Fortuner Neo Drive, though TKM has not confirmed this for the launched variants. An all-electric Hilux with a 59.2 kWh battery exists globally, but there is no timeline for its Indian debut, according to MotorBeam.

Competitive Landscape

The Hilux currently faces just one direct rival in India — the Isuzu D-Max V-Cross. That could change soon: Mahindra is developing a lifestyle pickup based on the Scorpio-N platform, which was previewed as the Global Pik-Up concept in South Africa, according to CarToq. The new 4x2 variant also puts the Hilux closer in price to large SUVs like the Toyota Fortuner and Skoda Kodiaq, potentially pulling in cross-shoppers.

What It Means for the Diaspora

For NRIs visiting India or maintaining property there, the Hilux occupies a unique space — a globally proven pickup with local service backing from Toyota's extensive dealer network, making it a practical choice for farmland, weekend homes, or adventure travel across the subcontinent.

What's Next

Test drives open across Toyota dealerships from July 29. TKM's next major launch will be a facelifted Innova Hycross, expected in early 2027, according to GaadiWaadi. The Hilux is available in six colour options, with EMIs starting at Rs 39,999 per month.
nri_angle: The Hilux offers NRIs a globally proven, Toyota-backed pickup option for Indian farmland, weekend properties, or adventure travel.
